stages.description: Load tiny reference tables into arrays, build filtered dimension structures and the shared European-partsupp join result. All operations are independent and run in parallel.

operations.notes: 25-entry array indexed by n_nationkey. Also derive: european_nation_bitset (n_regionkey matches EUROPE r_regionkey), asia_nation_bitset (ASIA), france_germany_pair_set (Q7), saudi_arabia_key (Q21), target_nation_key (Q20).
5-entry array. Used to resolve nation→region lookups for EUROPE (Q2,Q11), ASIA (Q5), AMERICA/MIDDLE EAST (Q8).

100K-entry array indexed by s_suppkey (dense_pk). Also build: Q16_excluded_supplier_bitset from s_comment LIKE '%Customer%Complaints%' (~4 suppliers). Supplier→nation mapping used in many lineitem-scan branches via s_nationkey array lookup.

Join partsupp with European suppliers (~20K of 100K). Build hash table keyed on ps_partkey for Q2 min-cost lookups. Q11 applies residual n_name='GERMANY' filter. Scan partsupp (8M rows) probing supplier array (dense_pk) → nation array → region array.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of lineitem (60M rows). The loop body contains 17 consumer branches. Each row is simultaneously evaluated against all active query filters. Dimension table lookups use dense_pk arrays (O(1)) for orders, customer, part, supplier. Partsupp probed via composite hash index for Q9.
stages.notes: Parallelize with OpenMP across row chunks (block_size=65536); each thread maintains thread-local accumulators and bitmaps; merge after the loop. AVX-512 can accelerate date comparisons and discount/quantity filters. All FK→PK lookups (orders, customer, part, supplier) use dense_pk arrays — no hash probes needed. Orders columns accessed via orders_pk_idx dense array; customer via customer_pk_idx; part via part_pk_idx; supplier via supplier_pk_idx.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate: group by (l_returnflag, l_linestatus) → sum qty, sum price, sum disc_price=price*(1-disc), sum charge=disc_price*(1+tax), count; 4 groups max, use fixed array
consumer_branches.notes: ~98.6% selectivity — nearly all rows qualify. Hot path.

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk[l_orderkey] → if o_orderdate < 729269 (1995-03-15) → probe customer_pk[o_custkey] → if c_mktsegment = BUILDING(dict_code) → accumulate revenue = l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount) into hash map keyed by (l_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_shippriority); maintain top-10 heap
consumer_branches.notes: ~51.3% lineitem selectivity × ~48.7% orders date × ~21% customer segment ≈ ~5.3% overall

consumer_branches.action: set bit in order_has_late_line bitset[l_orderkey]; used by Q4 main in orders scan
consumer_branches.notes: Bitset indexed by orderkey (max 60M keys → ~7.5MB). ~38% of lineitem rows satisfy commit < receipt.

consumer_branches.action: probe customer_pk[o_custkey] → lookup nation[c_nationkey] → if region = ASIA → lookup supplier[l_suppkey].s_nationkey → if supplier_nation == customer_nation → accumulate revenue by n_name
consumer_branches.notes: 5 groups (ASIA nations). ~15.7% orders date × ~20% ASIA customers × nation match ≈ ~0.6% overall

consumer_branches.filter: l_shipdate >= 727563 (1994-01-01) AND l_shipdate < 727928 (1995-01-01) AND l_discount BETWEEN 0.05 AND 0.07 AND l_quantity < 24
consumer_branches.action: accumulate scalar: sum(l_extendedprice * l_discount)
consumer_branches.notes: ~15.7% × 27.4% × 45.7% ≈ ~1.97% selectivity. Single scalar accumulator. Hot candidate for SIMD.

consumer_branches.action: probe supplier_pk[l_suppkey].s_nationkey → probe orders_pk[l_orderkey] → probe customer_pk[o_custkey].c_nationkey → lookup both nations → if (FRANCE,GERMANY) or (GERMANY,FRANCE) pair → accumulate volume by (supp_nation, cust_nation, l_year=extract_year(l_shipdate))
consumer_branches.notes: 4 result groups. ~31.4% date × ~0.16% nation pair ≈ ~0.05% overall

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk[l_orderkey] → if o_orderdate in [1995-01-01, 1996-12-31] → probe customer_pk[o_custkey] → lookup nation → lookup region → accumulate volume and brazil_volume by o_year=extract_year(o_orderdate)
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.7% part type × ~31.4% date ≈ ~0.22% overall. 2 result groups (years).

consumer_branches.filter: probe part_pk[l_partkey] → p_name contains 'green' (dictionary or substring check)
consumer_branches.action: probe partsupp_composite_hash[(l_partkey, l_suppkey)] → get ps_supplycost → probe supplier_pk[l_suppkey].s_nationkey → probe orders_pk[l_orderkey] → extract o_year → amount = l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount) - ps_supplycost*l_quantity → accumulate by (nation, o_year)
consumer_branches.notes: ~175 groups (25 nations × ~7 years). Part name filter ~0.7% selectivity.

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk[l_orderkey] → if o_orderdate in [1993-10-01, 1994-01-01) → probe customer_pk[o_custkey] → lookup nation[c_nationkey].n_name → accumulate revenue by (c_custkey, c_name, c_acctbal, c_phone, n_name, c_address, c_comment); maintain top-20 heap by revenue DESC
consumer_branches.notes: ~24.2% returnflag × ~3.9% orders date ≈ ~0.94%. High-cardinality grouping — use hash map with top-20 tracking.

consumer_branches.filter: l_shipmode IN ('MAIL','SHIP') AND l_receiptdate in [1994-01-01, 1995-01-01) AND l_commitdate < l_receiptdate AND l_shipdate < l_commitdate
consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk[l_orderkey] → get o_orderpriority → accumulate CASE(high_line_count if priority 1-URGENT or 2-HIGH, else low_line_count) by l_shipmode
consumer_branches.notes: ~28.6% shipmode × date/commit filters ≈ ~1.5%. 2 result groups.

consumer_branches.action: probe part_pk[l_partkey] → get p_type → accumulate sum(CASE WHEN p_type LIKE 'PROMO%' THEN l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount)) and sum(l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount))
consumer_branches.notes: ~1.3% date selectivity. 2 scalar accumulators.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) per l_suppkey into revenue array[100001]
consumer_branches.notes: ~3.9% date. 100K groups — use dense array indexed by s_suppkey. Max-revenue supplier found in finalize.

consumer_branches.filter: probe part_pk[l_partkey] → p_brand = 'Brand#23' AND p_container = 'MED BOX'
consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(l_quantity) and count per l_partkey into hash map → compute avg in post-step
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.1% of parts match (brand×container). Subquery accumulation. Main query re-scans matching partkeys via lineitem_partkey_grouped index in finalize stage.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(l_quantity) per l_orderkey into dense array[60000001] → post-filter: mark orderkeys where sum > 300
consumer_branches.notes: All 60M rows contribute. Dense array ~240MB (double per orderkey). Very few orders exceed qty 300 threshold. Heavy orderkey set used in orders scan.

consumer_branches.filter: l_shipmode IN ('AIR', 'AIR REG') AND l_shipinstruct = 'DELIVER IN PERSON'
consumer_branches.action: probe part_pk[l_partkey] → evaluate 3 OR-branches: (Brand#12 + SM containers + qty 1-11 + size 1-5) OR (Brand#23 + MED containers + qty 10-20 + size 1-10) OR (Brand#34 + LG containers + qty 20-30 + size 1-15) → accumulate sum(l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount))
consumer_branches.notes: ~28.6% shipmode × 25% shipinstruct × ~0.3% brand/container/size combos ≈ ~0.02%. Single scalar result.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(l_quantity) per (l_partkey, l_suppkey) into hash map
consumer_branches.notes: ~15.7% date selectivity. ~8M distinct (partkey,suppkey) pairs → hash map or use partsupp_composite_hash layout. Used in partsupp scan to compare against 0.5 * ps_availqty.

consumer_branches.action: probe orders_pk[l_orderkey] → if o_orderstatus = 'F' → probe supplier_pk[l_suppkey].s_nationkey → if nation = SAUDI ARABIA → record (l_orderkey, l_suppkey) as candidate; also for ALL rows on 'F' orders: track per-orderkey supplier sets and late-supplier sets for multi-supplier / no-other-late checks
consumer_branches.notes: Complex: for each 'F' order, need to know (1) total distinct suppliers, (2) which suppliers were late, (3) which of those are from SAUDI ARABIA. Build per-orderkey structures: suppkey_count, late_suppkey_set. Evaluate in finalize: exists other supplier AND no other late supplier.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of orders (15M rows). Uses intermediate results from lineitem scan (Q4 bitmap, Q18 heavy orderkeys, Q21 supplier info). Also drives Q13 order-per-customer counting.
stages.notes: Parallelize with OpenMP across row chunks; thread-local accumulators merged after loop. Q13 needs the varlen o_comment column for NOT LIKE check — may be I/O-heavy on HDD. Orders sorted by o_orderkey enabling sequential access to Q4/Q18/Q21 intermediates indexed by orderkey.

consumer_branches.action: check q4_order_has_late_line_bitset[o_orderkey] → if set → accumulate count by o_orderpriority
consumer_branches.notes: ~3.9% date selectivity. 5 result groups.

consumer_branches.action: increment orders_per_customer[o_custkey] counter (dense array[1500001]). In finalize: build histogram of c_count values across all 1.5M customers
consumer_branches.notes: ~99.4% pass the NOT LIKE filter. Dense array ~6MB. Histogram built in finalize by iterating array.

consumer_branches.action: probe customer_pk[o_custkey] → accumulate (c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice, sum_qty from subquery); maintain top-100 heap by o_totalprice DESC, o_orderdate ASC
consumer_branches.notes: Very few qualifying orderkeys (~57 at SF10). Effectively a sparse probe — most rows skip immediately.

consumer_branches.action: for qualifying orderkeys from q21_order_supplier_info: evaluate multi-supplier + single-late-Saudi conditions → accumulate count by s_name
consumer_branches.notes: ~33% orderstatus='F'. Cross-reference with per-order supplier tracking from lineitem scan. ~4000 result groups.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of partsupp (8M rows). Drives Q16 (distinct supplier count by part attributes) and Q20 (supplier availability check). Q2 and Q11 use the pre-built European join result instead.
stages.notes: Parallelize with OpenMP across row chunks. Sorted by (ps_partkey, ps_suppkey) enabling sequential part_pk lookups. Q16 needs COUNT(DISTINCT ps_suppkey) — use hash sets per group. Q20 probes lineitem subquery results.

consumer_branches.action: probe part_pk[ps_partkey] → if p_brand != 'Brand#45' AND p_type NOT LIKE 'MEDIUM POLISHED%' AND p_size IN (49,14,23,45,19,3,36,9) → insert ps_suppkey into per-(p_brand, p_type, p_size) distinct set
consumer_branches.notes: ~96% brand × ~96% type × ~16% size ≈ ~14.7%. High-cardinality grouping — use hash map of (brand,type,size) → HyperLogLog or hash set for distinct count.

consumer_branches.action: lookup q20_partsupp_qty_sums[(ps_partkey, ps_suppkey)] → if sum > 0.5 * ps_availqty → probe supplier_pk[ps_suppkey].s_nationkey → if nation = target_nation → collect (s_name, s_address) for output
consumer_branches.notes: ~0.7% part name × nation filter ≈ very selective. Result sorted by s_name in finalize.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of the pre-built European partsupp join result (1.6M rows). Feeds Q2 (min-cost supplier per part) and Q11 (value by partkey for Germany).
stages.notes: Small enough to fit in L3 cache. No OpenMP needed — single-threaded is likely faster due to low row count and cache residency.

consumer_branches.filter: probe part_pk[ps_partkey] → p_size = 15 AND p_type LIKE '%BRASS'
consumer_branches.action: for each qualifying part: track minimum ps_supplycost per ps_partkey in hash map; on second mini-pass (or deferred comparison in finalize): output rows where ps_supplycost = min for that partkey; collect (s_acctbal, s_name, n_name, p_partkey, p_mfgr, s_address, s_phone, s_comment); top-100 by s_acctbal DESC, n_name, s_name, p_partkey
consumer_branches.notes: ~2% size × ~4% type ≈ ~0.08% of parts qualify. Two-phase: first pass tracks min cost per partkey, second pass collects matching rows.

consumer_branches.action: accumulate sum(ps_supplycost * ps_availqty) per ps_partkey into hash map; also accumulate global_total for threshold (fraction × total); in finalize: filter partkeys where value > threshold, sort by value DESC
consumer_branches.notes: ~4% nation filter (1 of 25 nations in Europe subset = 1/5). ~320K rows from Germany.

stages.description: Single-pass scan of customer (1.5M rows) for Q22. Only consumer — but cannot be folded into another scan since Q22's driving table is customer.
stages.notes: Two-phase within single scan: Phase 1 computes avg(c_acctbal) for customers with positive balance AND phone code in target set. Phase 2 (or combined with deferred evaluation in finalize) checks each candidate against avg threshold and order-existence via custkey_to_orders index.

consumer_branches.action: Phase 1: if c_acctbal > 0 → accumulate sum and count for avg threshold. Phase 2: if c_acctbal > avg_threshold → check custkey_to_orders index for order existence → if no orders → accumulate count and sum(c_acctbal) by country_code = SUBSTRING(c_phone,1,2)
probes_tables: orders(custkey_to_orders index for existence check only)
consumer_branches.notes: ~28% phone code filter. 7 result groups. Two-pass over customer data or single pass collecting candidates + deferred threshold application in finalize.

stages.description: Per-query finalization: compute derived results, sort, limit, format, write CSV. Each query finalizes independently. Queries with intermediate results do their final computation here.

operations.action: compute averages (sum/count); sort by (l_returnflag ASC, l_linestatus ASC) → output CSV (4 rows)
from min-cost tracking: collect rows where supplycost = min for partkey; sort by (s_acctbal DESC, n_name, s_name, p_partkey); LIMIT 100 → output CSV
extract top-10 from heap by (revenue DESC, o_orderdate ASC) → output CSV
sort 5 groups by o_orderpriority ASC → output CSV
sort 5 groups by revenue DESC → output CSV
output single-row CSV (scalar sum)
sort 4 groups by (supp_nation, cust_nation, l_year) ASC → output CSV
compute mkt_share = brazil_volume / total_volume per year; sort by o_year ASC → output CSV (2 rows)
sort ~175 groups by (nation ASC, o_year DESC) → output CSV
extract top-20 from heap by revenue DESC → output CSV
compute threshold = 0.0001 * global_total; filter partkeys where value > threshold; sort by value DESC → output CSV
sort 2 groups by l_shipmode ASC → output CSV
iterate orders_per_customer array (1.5M entries, including zeros); build histogram of c_count → sort by (custdist DESC, c_count DESC) → output CSV (~40 rows)
compute 100.0 * promo_sum / total_sum → output single-row CSV
find max revenue in supplier_revenue array; scan for supplier(s) matching max; join with supplier for output columns; output CSV sorted by s_suppkey ASC
finalize distinct counts per (brand,type,size) group; sort by (supplier_cnt DESC, p_brand, p_type, p_size) → output CSV

compute avg_qty per partkey from Q17_sub sums/counts; re-scan matching lineitem rows via lineitem_partkey_grouped index where l_quantity < 0.2 * avg_qty; accumulate sum(l_extendedprice) / 7.0 → output single-row CSV
extract top-100 from heap by (o_totalprice DESC, o_orderdate ASC); for each, join l_quantity sum from subquery → output CSV
output single-row CSV (scalar sum)
sort qualifying suppliers by s_name ASC → output CSV
from per-order supplier analysis: for each SAUDI ARABIAN supplier with qualifying orders, count occurrences; sort by (numwait DESC, s_name ASC); LIMIT 100 → output CSV
sort 7 groups by cntrycode ASC → output CSV

parallelism_opportunities: fused_scan_european_partsupp and scan_customer_q22 can run in parallel with fused_scan_lineitem (no data dependencies)
fused_scan_orders and fused_scan_partsupp can run in parallel after fused_scan_lineitem completes (independent consumers)
Within each fused scan: OpenMP parallel for across row chunks (block_size=65536), thread-local accumulators merged post-loop
